title.narrative: 1.1. Percentage of citizens who say they are aware and comply with healthrelated measures to prevent the spread of COVID19

description.narrative: % of Montenegrin citizens that are aware and adhering to ALL preventive measures: frequent handwashing, physical distancing and wearing masks indoor.

comment.narrative: Baseline survey available from httpswww.unicef.orgmontenegroenmedia17531fileMontenegro27scitizens27viewsonvaccinesandCOVID19.pdf
Final target has been set to 15 increase of the baseline values 24 months from project start.

The indicator value has been very difficult to track and monitor as public health measures and recommendations have been extremely dynamic and have changed numerous times over the Action implementation and especially during winter and then summer touristic season of 20212022.In COVID19 general population health tracker conducted by IPSOS in June 2021 76 53 increase of total target population personally applied and followed measures and recommendation on personal protection that were valid at that time wearing a face mask and keeping the distance.Based on previously established criteria and following the recommendations of the Emergency Committee the WHO Director General on May 5th 2023 declared an end to the COVID19 public health emergency of international concern PHEIC which was active since January 30th 2020. This decision significantly dropped global public perception of COVID19 as an imminent individual and public health threat which consequently led to drop in adherence to recommendations and followingup of the preventive measures leaving COVID19 reasonably out the primary focus of the Action during the third year of implementation. The reported value represents proportion of general Montenegrin population who said that they follow are aware and comply with healthrelated measures to prevent the spread of COVID19 as measured in public perception survey in July 2021. Reported value reflects the increase of 13 from baseline

National coordinating body for infectious diseases has been established on the basis of Article 56 of the Regulation on the Organization and Mode of Operation of the State Administration which prescribed that for the performance of tasks within which professional cooperation is required civil servants from different internal organizational units can educateproject groups teams or other appropriate forms of work and that the project group team or the second form of work consists of in addition to the Vice President of the Government of Montenegro and the Minister that is the head of the administrative body.Over the time some of the jurisdictions of the Council were gradually taken by the Government and Prime minister himself. In the last half of 2022 and by the time when COVID19 was not considered as PHEIC and mainly due to the favorable epidemiological situation Council didnt have significant media visibility nor important meetings. Officially Council has been resolved of the duties by Governments decision on May 26th 2023.Comments on functioning of the Body are available in EU repots on Montenegrin progress towards the European Union accession process httpswww.eeas.europa.eusitesdefaultfilesizvjestajmne2020.pdf

title.narrative: I1: Rate of new COVID19 infections maintained under control

description.narrative: Number of COVID19 cases in Montenegro is at, or below, EU average at the end of the Action 36 months from project start, indicating that disease spread is under control.

comment.narrative: At the time of Action proposal development end Nov 2020 biweekly rate of COVID19 active cases in Montenegro has been around 12.000 per 1 million population high above EU average. At the same time the 14day case notification rate for the EUEEA and the UK based on data collected by ECDC from official national sources from 31 countries was 5490 country range 580 11860 per 1 million population.At the end of Action biweekly rates of new COVID19 cases per one million inhabitants were 448 in Montenegro and 5188 in EU average.

At the end of Action implementation January 2024 biweekly rate of COVID19 active cases in Montenegro has been around 448 per 1 million population while at the same time EU average has been around 5188 active COVID19 cases.

Target indicator value has been number of COVID19 cases disease under control at or below EU average 36 months from project start. Based on the described data portals and reports at the end of project implementation EU has been experiencing 5188 Biweekly cases per 1M population while the rate for the same period of time for Montenegro has been 448 biweekly COVID19 cases per 1 million population.

title.narrative: I2: Coverage of MMR1 (measles, mumps, rubella) vaccine

description.narrative: Percentage of children immunized against measles, mumps and rubella.

comment.narrative: Baseline indicator refers to vaccine coverage of children born in 2018 that has been achieved in January 2021.
Final target refers to the MMR1 coverages achieved among cohort of children aged three children born in 2020 at the end of Action implementation January 2024.

Thanks to supplementary activities and intensification of routine immunizations provided through this Action coverages both in terms of MMR1 timeliness and completeness have improved but still remain far from desirable. MMR1 coverage in the birth cohort that has been used as baseline cohort 2018 has reached targeted indicator values in January 2023 of 753.Coverages among other birth cohorts in January 2024 are as following2018 79202019 74032020 65192021 4499This indicates that the longterm sustainability of the results achieved might be jeopardized if continuation of capacity building of healthcare workers and other interventions are not continued in years to come based on data and evidence generated through research.As the indicator end value has been set for the cohort of 2020 at the end of project implementation indicator value reported here reflects MMR1 coverage achieved by January 2024 among children born in 2020.

title.narrative: IPA PF 2.11 Number of public policies developed and/or revised with internal and external consultations with EU support

description.narrative: SDG 16 Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levelsPublic policies are understood in a broad manner, including Government programme, strategies, administrative acts and legislations at national or subnational levels.

comment.narrative: National Action plan for immunizations catchup plan municipal supplementary immunization action plans immunization SOPs Immunization supportive supervision plan and other documents have been developed either through internal ministries other public entities andor external CSO consultative process participation.

National Action plan for immunizations catchup plan has been developed as part of this Action through internal two Ministries public health entities UN agencies and external CSO participation with EU support. At the same time various other documents including municipal supplementary immunization action plans immunization SOPs Immunization supportive supervision plan... have been developed within the Action with EU support mostly through internal consultative participation process. As these documents do not fulfill the definition of subnational policies as they were not expected to be endorsed by the relevant local authorities and were not reported in indicator values.

description.narrative: Percentage of children immunized against measles, mumps and rubella.

comment.narrative: Baseline indicator refers to vaccine coverage of children born in 2018 that has been achieved in January 2021.
Final target refers to the MMR1 coverages achieved among cohort of children aged three children born in 2020 at the end of Action implementation January 2024.

Thanks to supplementary activities and intensification of routine immunizations provided through this Action coverages both in terms of MMR1 timeliness and completeness have improved but still remain far from desirable. MMR1 coverage in the birth cohort that has been used as baseline cohort 2018 has reached targeted indicator values in January 2023 of 753.Coverages among other birth cohorts in January 2024 are as following2018 79202019 74032020 65192021 4499This indicates that the longterm sustainability of the results achieved might be jeopardized if continuation of capacity building of healthcare workers and other interventions are not continued in years to come based on data and evidence generated through research.As the indicator end value has been set for the cohort of 2020 at the end of project implementation indicator value reported here reflects MMR1 coverage achieved by January 2024 among children born in 2020.
